template_name: Sharp-Wave Ripple Replay and Spatial Memory Consolidation
calibration_constraint: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT for human architectural translation; animal mechanism confidence can be high

mechanism_chain.process: During quiet wakefulness, hippocampus transitions from theta state (8–12 Hz, active exploration) to large irregular activity (LIA) characterized by sharp-wave ripple complexes (SWRs: 150–250 Hz oscillation lasting 50–120 ms)
mechanism_chain.substrate: CA3 excitatory burst → CA1 sharp-wave; CA1 pyramidal-interneuron interaction generates ripple

data.finding: Sharp-wave ripples (150-250 Hz, 50-120 ms) are the characteristic hippocampal oscillation during quiet wakefulness and NREM sleep
SWRs are generated by CA3 excitatory burst propagating to CA1; ripple oscillation arises from pyramidal-interneuron interaction

justification.backing: Buzsáki's work established the SWR as the signature hippocampal oscillation for offline processing. The theta → LIA transition is behaviorally gated: active exploration maintains theta, while quiet wakefulness enables SWR generation.
justification.qualifier: The SWR mechanism is established in rodents. Human hippocampal oscillations are less directly measurable; fMRI and iEEG provide indirect evidence.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human hippocampal offline states differ fundamentally from rodent; but intracranial EEG evidence supports SWR-like activity in human hippocampus.

mechanism_chain.process: During each SWR event, recent spatial experience is replayed in compressed temporal sequence: place cells that were active during navigation fire in the same sequence but compressed to ~20× real time
mechanism_chain.substrate: CA3 → CA1 replay sequences; compressed temporal code

data.finding: Place cells replay recent navigation sequences during SWRs in compressed temporal order (20× compression)
Both forward and reverse replay occur during SWRs; reverse replay may support learning from recent experience

justification.backing: Lee and Wilson's demonstration of compressed sequential replay during SWRs provided the key evidence linking SWRs to memory consolidation. The 20× temporal compression enables rapid repeated replay of extended spatial experiences.
justification.qualifier: Replay has been demonstrated primarily in rodent navigation paradigms. The generalization to human spatial memory consolidation is inferred.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human spatial memory consolidation uses different mechanisms than rodent; but fMRI evidence of hippocampal replay signatures supports translation.

mechanism_chain.process: SWR replay drives synaptic plasticity in neocortical target regions: each replay event strengthens the cortico-cortical connections that will eventually store the spatial memory independently of hippocampus
mechanism_chain.substrate: Hippocampal → entorhinal → neocortical Hebbian plasticity during replay
mechanism_chain.source: Girardeau et al. (2009); Jadhav et al. (2012)

data.finding: SWRs are coupled with cortical activity patterns; replay during SWRs drives neocortical plasticity
data.source: Girardeau et al. (2009); Peyrache et al. (2009)

data.finding: Repeated SWR replay gradually strengthens neocortical representations, enabling eventual hippocampal-independent retrieval
data.source: Standard model of consolidation; Frankland & Bontempi (2005)

justification.backing: The systems consolidation model proposes that SWR replay drives Hebbian plasticity in neocortex. Repeated replay gradually strengthens cortico-cortical connections until the memory can be retrieved without hippocampal involvement.
justification.qualifier: The plasticity mechanism is inferred from correlational evidence (SWR-cortical coupling predicts memory). Direct measurement of synapse-level changes during replay is limited.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if consolidation occurs through non-replay mechanisms; but SWR disruption impairs consolidation, supporting the causal role of replay.

mechanism_chain.process: Disrupting SWRs during rest impairs spatial memory consolidation: animals with SWR disruption show impaired performance on subsequent navigation tasks

data.finding: Closed-loop SWR disruption during post-learning rest impairs subsequent spatial memory performance
SWR disruption selectively impairs recently acquired spatial memories; older memories are unaffected
data.paradigm: SWR disruption with varying retention intervals

justification.backing: The causal necessity of SWRs for spatial memory consolidation is established by disruption studies. Selectively preventing SWRs during the consolidation window impairs memory without affecting older, already-consolidated memories.
justification.qualifier: Disruption studies are in rodents. Human translation relies on the assumption that human spatial memory consolidation similarly depends on SWR-like mechanisms.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if humans use SWR-independent consolidation mechanisms for spatial memory; but indirect evidence supports similar mechanisms.

mechanism_chain.process: Environmental conditions for SWR generation: quiet wakefulness in a familiar, low-complexity environment. Locomotion, high visual complexity, salient stimuli, and demanding cognitive tasks suppress SWRs by maintaining the hippocampus in theta state.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Behavioral state → hippocampal oscillatory state transition

data.finding: Locomotion and active exploration maintain hippocampal theta; cessation of movement allows transition to LIA/SWR state
Salient stimuli and cognitive demand suppress SWRs by maintaining arousal and theta

justification.backing: The behavioral gating of SWR generation provides the bridge to architectural design: environments that promote quiet wakefulness (low arousal, minimal cognitive demand, familiarity) enable the theta → LIA transition necessary for SWR generation and memory consolidation.
justification.qualifier: The behavioral gating is established; the specific environmental features that modulate arousal and cognitive demand in architectural contexts involve capacity assumptions.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human state transitions are less sensitive to environmental conditions than rodent; or if internal factors (mood, fatigue) dominate environmental influences.

memory_consolidation.interpretation: Individual SWRs cannot be reliably detected with scalp EEG. Human evidence relies on fMRI DMN re-engagement as proxy for hippocampal replay. The translation from rodent SWR to human architectural rest is THEORETICAL_DEFAULT.

temporal_rhythm.interpretation: Minimum rest period required for meaningful SWR-mediated replay. Shorter periods produce some SWRs but insufficient replay for measurable consolidation benefit.

animal_mechanism_confidence.interpretation: The SWR replay mechanism in rodents is well-established with causal evidence (disruption studies). This is separate from the human architectural translation confidence.

age_group.effect: SWR frequency and amplitude decline with age; coupling with cortical slow oscillations degrades. Elderly adults may need LONGER rest periods for equivalent replay benefit.

arousal_level.effect: Sympathetic nervous system activation suppresses SWRs by maintaining hippocampal theta. Environments that induce arousal (noise, threat, crowding) prevent the theta → LIA transition required for replay.

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Body budget restoration and SWR replay share environmental conditions: both require low arousal, comfort, and absence of threat. Restorative environments that restore body budget (per IC2) simultaneously create conditions for SWR replay. This is a mechanistic convergence, not a coincidence — both processes require parasympathetic dominance.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: High perceived control reduces vigilance and facilitates the relaxed wakefulness state that supports SWR generation. Low perceived control maintains sympathetic tone and hippocampal theta, suppressing replay.

cross_template_references: ED_SYSTEMS_CONSOLIDATION_001 — SWR replay is the primary driver of systems consolidation
MS_CONSOLIDATION_RESTORATION_001 — DMN re-engagement during rest complements SWR replay
STRESS-I T6 — cortisol and sympathetic activation suppress SWR generation
VISUAL-I VIEW1 — nature view channels 1–3 support consolidation-permissive state

visual_complexity.interpretation: High visual complexity (SRV > 0.15) suppresses the theta → LIA transition by maintaining attentional engagement; negative coefficient reduces SWR probability

acoustic_environment.interpretation: Effective acoustic shielding (STC ≥ 45) supports the quiet wakefulness state required for SWR generation

nature_view_quality.interpretation: Nature views promote soft fascination (Kaplan, 1995) — a state of diffuse attention compatible with DMN re-engagement and SWR generation
